proposition: A contractual choice yields to the law of a state with a materially greater interest and fundamental contrary policy when that state's law would otherwise apply.
Texas refused a foreign law clause in a non-compete dispute because the working state had a materially greater interest and contrary fundamental policy.

cite: Nedlloyd Lines B.V. v. Superior Court, 3 Cal.4th 459 (1992)
proposition: California applies the Restatement §187 fundamental-policy and materially-greater-interest test to contractual law choices.

cite: Application Group, Inc. v. Hunter Group, Inc., 61 Cal.App.4th 881 (1998)
proposition: California's non-compete policy is fundamental and displaced a foreign law choice where California had a materially greater interest.

An employee who primarily resides and works in California can elect to void prohibited, required out-of-state forum and choice provisions; actual individual counsel in negotiation is an exception; employee fees are discretionary.

cite: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code §17.042; Michiana Easy Livin' Country v. Holten, 168 S.W.3d 777 (Tex. 2005)
proposition: A forum clause generally supplies jurisdictional consent, but independent Texas contacts become uncertain if it is voided; a Texas injunction faces California nonrecognition risk.

cite: Advanced Bionics Corp. v. Medtronic, Inc., 29 Cal.4th 697 (2002)
proposition: California courts generally should not enjoin parallel litigation in another state over a non-compete.

cite: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §16600 (as amended by SB 699, eff. Jan. 1, 2024)
proposition: Employment non-competes are void absent a statutory exception, regardless of narrow tailoring.

cite: Edwards v. Arthur Andersen LLP, 44 Cal.4th 937 (2008)
proposition: California rejects the narrow-restraint exception for employment non-competes.

cite: Ixchel Pharma, LLC v. Biogen, Inc., 9 Cal.5th 1130 (2020)
proposition: A rule of reason for business-to-business restraints is distinct from the rule governing employment non-competes.
Void non-competes are unenforceable regardless of signing place; entry or attempted enforcement is a civil violation with employee injunctive, damages, and prevailing-party fee remedies.
An employment covenant must be ancillary and reasonably limited; the employer bears the burden; courts must reform unreasonable limits and cannot award prereformation breach damages.

cite: Alex Sheshunoff Management Services, L.P. v. Johnson, 209 S.W.3d 644 (Tex. 2006)
proposition: An employer's promise to provide confidential information can support an at-will employment covenant when the promise is later performed.

cite: Marsh USA Inc. v. Cook, 354 S.W.3d 764 (Tex. 2011)
proposition: Stock-option consideration related to goodwill can support a covenant without a narrow give-rise requirement.

cite: FTC Non-Compete Clause Rule, 89 Fed. Reg. 38342 (May 7, 2024)
proposition: The final federal non-compete rule was vacated nationwide and never took effect.

cite: Ryan LLC v. FTC, 739 F. Supp. 3d 496 (N.D. Tex. 2024)
proposition: The district court set aside the FTC Non-Compete Clause Rule nationwide; the appeal was later dismissed.
Invalid non-competes cannot be included in employment contracts; individualized notices to eligible workers were due February 14, 2024, and violation is unfair competition.
